facts.statement: The genus was described in 2011 by Alexander K. Hastings, Jonathan Bloch, and Carlos A. Jaramillo from fossils found in the Cerrejón coal mine in northeastern Colombia.
facts.quote: All Acherontisuchus specimens were collected from the Cerrejón Formation within the Cerrejón coal mine of northeastern Colombia and described in 2011 in Palaeontology journal by Alexander K. Hastings, Jonathan Bloch and Carlos A. Jaramillo.

facts.statement: It is classified as a long-snouted dyrosaurid.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus is considered a long-snouted, or longirostrine, dyrosaurid.

facts.statement: The upper jaw was wide rather than high.
facts.quote: The upper jaw is wide rather than high.

facts.statement: Its head is estimated to have been 72 to 86 cm long, which is about midsize for a dyrosaurid.
facts.quote: Its head is estimated to have been 72 - 86 cm long, about midsize for a dyrosaurid.

facts.statement: It lived in Middle to Late Paleocene deposits of Colombia.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus is an extinct genus of dyrosaurid neosuchian from Middle to Late Paleocene deposits of Colombia.

facts.statement: It lived in South America during the Paleocene, approximately 60 million years ago.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus es el nombre de un género extinto de crocodilomorfo prehistórico perteneciente a la familia de los dirosáuridos que vivió en el período Paleoceno, hace unos 60 millones de años, en América del Sur.

facts.statement: It lived in calm, shallow, inland freshwater habitats within the tropical rainforests of northeastern Colombia.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus lived in a calm, shallow, inland freshwater habitat in the tropical rainforests of northeastern Colombia, where its distant cousin Cerrejonisuchus lived as well.

facts.statement: Its slender ischial shaft suggests that the muscles controlling its position in water were less developed than in oceanic relatives.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus has a slender ischial shaft, suggesting that the muscles that controlled its position in water were less developed.

facts.statement: It most likely fed on lungfishes and eels in inland rivers.
facts.quote: In these inland rivers, Acherontisuchus most likely fed on lungfishes and eels.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places it in a derived clade of dyrosaurids alongside Hyposaurus, Congosaurus, Atlantosuchus, Rhabdognathus, and Guarinisuchus.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis conducted with its first description placed Acherontisuchus in a derived clade of dyrosaurids that included Hyposaurus of North America, Congosaurus, Atlantosuchus, and Rhabdognathus of Africa, and Guarinisuchus of South America.

facts.statement: It was named after the river Acheron, a branch of the river Styx in Greek mythology meaning "river of woe", referencing its habitat in a large river emptying into the Caribbean Sea.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado por el río Aqueronte, el cual en la mitología griega era un brazo del río Estigia que significa "río del dolor", haciendo referencia a que se piensa que Acherontisuchus vivió en un gran río que desembocaba en el mar Caribe durante el Paleoceno.

facts.statement: The type species A. guajiraensis is named after the Guajira Peninsula where the Cerrejón mine is located.
facts.quote: La especie tipo A. guajiraensis fue nombrada por la península de la Guajira en la que se localiza la mina del Cerrejón.

facts.statement: Aside from consistently fractured fossils, there is no evidence that fossil size has been altered.
facts.quote: Aparte de los consistentemente fracturados fósiles, no existe evidencia de que se haya alterado el tamaño del fósil.

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus lived between 61.66 and 56 million years ago during the Selandian to Thanetian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Thanetian (61.66 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Acherontisuchus was described by Hastings and colleagues in 2011.
facts.quote: Hastings et al. 2011

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus belongs to the subfamily Hyposaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hyposaurinae

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus is classified within the family Dyrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dyrosauridae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Acherontisuchus is Acherontisuchus guajiraensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Acherontisuchus guajiraensis

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus is a member of the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus lived in a freshwater and tropical rainforest habitat in northern Colombia.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus vivió en un hábitat de agua dulce y de selva tropical que existieron en el norte de Colombia en esa época

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus primarily ate fish, aided by its long, narrow snout which was similar to that of modern false gharials.
facts.quote: alimentándose primordialmente de peces gracias a su hocico largo y estrecho, algo similar al de los actuales falsos gaviales

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus had a thin ischial axis, suggesting that the muscles controlling its position in the water were less developed.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus tenían un delgado eje isquial, lo que sugiere que los músculos que controlan su posición en el agua estaban menos desarrollados

facts.statement: Based on the shape of its ribs and limb bones, Acherontisuchus likely had strong muscles along its back and legs to allow movement on land.
facts.quote: Basándose en la forma de sus costillas y huesos de sus extremidades, Acherontisuchus probablemente tenía fuertes músculos a lo largo de su espalda y en sus piernas como para permitirle moverse en tierra

facts.statement: In these inland rivers, Acherontisuchus likely fed on dipnoan fish and eels.
facts.quote: En estos ríos de tierra adentro, Acherontisuchus probablemente se alimentaba de peces dipnoos y anguilas

facts.statement: This large crocodyliform coexisted with Titanoboa, the largest known snake weighing 1.2 tons, with which it may have occasionally competed for food.
facts.quote: Este crocodilomorfo grande coexistía con la serpiente más grande conocida en el mundo, Titanoboa de 1,2 toneladas de peso, con la que pudo haber competido ocasionalmente por el alimento

facts.statement: Hastings suggested that while juvenile Acherontisuchus likely faced risks from Titanoboa, adults might have been too large for the 13-meter snake to prey upon.
facts.quote: Hastings escribió: "Con seguridad, los ejemplares más jóvenes corrían riesgos con Titanoboa, pero los más grandes podrían haber sido demasiado para la serpiente de 13 metros."

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus is closely related to other dyrosaurids found in both Africa and America.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus está cercanamente relacionado con otros dirosáuridos tanto de África como de América

facts.statement: Acherontisuchus possessed several primitive features distinguishing it from other derived dyrosaurids, including uniformly spaced teeth and a wide connection between the two halves of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Acherontisuchus tenía varias características primitivas que lo distancian de otros miembros del derivado clado de dirosáuridos, incluyendo dientes uniformemente espaciados y una amplia conexión entre las dos mitades de la mandíbula inferior

facts.statement: Because relationships among dyrosaurids are not well resolved, Acherontisuchus was placed in a polytomy with Hyposaurus, Congosaurus, and a group containing other close relatives.
facts.quote: Las relaciones entre los dirosáuridos no están bien resueltas, por lo que Acherontisuchus fue colocado en una politomía con Hyposaurus, Congosaurus, y un grupo que contiene a otros parientes cercanos
